meaning: A shiny disc that held computer files, like programs or whole encyclopedias. A computer could read it but not change it.
clues: It is a shiny disc you slide into a computer.
It holds files and programs, up to about 700 megabytes, and a computer can only read it, not save new things on it.
Games and big books of facts came on one disc.
Your computer needed a special drive with a tray that slid out.
It has two parts joined by a hyphen. The second part stands for "read-only memory".
assumes: A DVD holds movies and more data than a CD
A Zip disk is a thick removable disk

decoys.meaning: A shiny disc that holds music for a CD player.
A shiny disc that holds movies and more data than a CD.
A thick removable disk that held far more than a floppy disk.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: One of those discs held more than a hundred of me. I was jealous and impressed.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: downloads and online libraries. A USB flash drive can still carry files from one computer to another.
